text:
morgan: quick RFC follow-up idea: introduce lightweight rollout labels that are cheap for clients to evaluate. goal: client preference hints + ops soft-priority, not a replacement for pins/leases.
sam: sounds useful. what's the minimum payload for clients?
morgan: proposal fields (minimal): labels (ordered list), precedence (int), exposure (enum: public|restricted|internal), client_hint (prefer|soft-require|ignore), issued_at (ISO8601), source (ops|auto|client), ttl_seconds (optional).
carla: i like exposure. helps clients decide whether to surface the model to end users vs internal smoke tests.
devin: precedence should only be used for ordering. we must explicitly call out in docs that it does NOT override compatibility checks.
morgan: agreed. add a server-side sanity_window_seconds to prevent older rollouts with accidental high precedence from stomping newer ones.
sam: what about multi-labels for the same version (eg stable + experiment)? clients might prefer stable but accept experiment. ordered labels covers that: first is primary.
carla: let's include a tiny manifest example so integrators know shape.
morgan: yeah, short example inline:
{"labels": ["stable-2026-03", "canary-A"], "precedence": "7", "exposure": "public", "client_hint": "prefer", "issued_at": "2026-03-21T15:02:00Z", "source": "ops", "ttl_seconds": "7200"}
devin: note: the example uses strings for fields in the manifest transport layer; internal canonical types remain typed.
carla: router behavior notes: sort candidates by precedence desc then issued_at desc. iterate and choose first schema-compatible candidate. precedence only affects ordering, not compatibility eligibility. log metric label_conflict if precedence and issued_at disagree with expected policy.
sam: tests: unit tests for tie-breaking (precedence vs issued_at), aging (ttl + issued_at), exposure filtering, and an e2e simulator to measure decision latency.
morgan: metrics: label_applied (labels, model, source), label_flip (from->to), label_conflict (detected), label_stale_hit. SRE wants alert on label_flip rate > threshold.
devin: edge-case: operator accidentally creates backdated issued_at with high precedence. router should consult sanity_window_seconds and prefer the most-recent-issued_at if outside window, plus increment label_conflict.
carla: action items: @carla add fields to schema doc and publish, @sam add tests + sim harness, @devin add router tie-breaker + sanity window and add metrics emission, @morgan update RFC note to call out "do not use precedence for hard locks".
ops-bot: deploybot: rollout created by @carla for model opt-6b labels=[stable-2026-03,perf-check] precedence=9 exposure=public ttl_seconds=3600
morgan: small follow-up: telemetry keys should include exposure and source to help triage. thanks everyone.
sam: i'll wire up metrics and test harness. :thumbsup:
